issues.title: [M-04B organ] Deployment and proving grounds
issues.purpose: Provides real populations, operational environments, conflicts, borders, agencies, and institutions in which systems are deployed, adapted, and validated.

issues.title: [M-04B organ] Residual rights and ownership

issues.title: [M-04B organ] Counterpower, inspection, and exit
issues.purpose: Audits, adjudicates, appeals, substitutes, terminates, migrates, corrects, or otherwise limits the architecture.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Common purpose
issues.purpose: Actor-specific doctrine and strategy converge on the same institutional future and are connected to organizational action.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Organ differentiation
issues.purpose: Nominally separate entities deliberately perform complementary, nonredundant functions in the same operating chain.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Resource metabolism
issues.purpose: Public authority, data, risk, subsidy, and demand repeatedly flow into private revenue, equity, rights, and renewed gate-shaping capacity.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Coordination and integration
issues.purpose: Governance, capital, personnel, contracts, APIs, interoperability records, or joint operations connect the organs.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Institutional reproduction
issues.purpose: The network repeatedly creates new companies, vehicles, banks, cohorts, or standards that fill missing functions in the architecture.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Feedback and adaptation
issues.purpose: Operational results in one theater measurably alter product design, doctrine, procurement, standards, financing, or deployment elsewhere.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Strategic invisibility and accountability membrane
issues.purpose: Legal, semantic, contractual, geographic, or organizational fragmentation systematically prevents end-to-end reconstruction while preserving integrated function.

issues.title: [M-04B test] Coercive governance and extraction
issues.purpose: The integrated system materially constrains populations or institutions while private actors retain disproportionate authority or residual value.
